prompt.context_jp: 深夜の桑野の仕事部屋には、青白い蛍光灯の光___静かに落ちていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 深夜の桑野の仕事部屋には、青白い蛍光灯の光___静かに落ちていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that best fits the blank.

feedback.correct_en: This is a scene-setting description introducing the light as new information in the narrative — が marks the newly presented subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'the light' a familiar topic being commented on, which doesn't fit this opening descriptive moment. を is wrong because 落ちる here is intransitive.

contrast_examples.jp: 光は差し込まなかった。
contrast_examples.en: The light (which we were discussing) didn't stream in.

prompt.context_jp: 客の要望と桑野の主張のあいだを取り持つの___、いつも英治の役目だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 客の要望と桑野の主張のあいだを取り持つの___、いつも英治の役目だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that best fits the blank.

feedback.correct_en: The nominalized clause is the topic being characterized ('as for mediating… it was Eiji's role'). は sets it up as the theme.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present it as new identifying information, but here the sentence is explaining a known situation, not identifying who does something out of alternatives.

contrast_examples.en: Eiji does the mediating. (new info / who)

prompt.context_jp: 「別に… だってさ 家で待ってんの___ 人だけとは限らないんだぞ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 家で待ってんの___ 人だけとは限らないんだぞ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that best fits the blank.

feedback.correct_en: Kuwano is making a general statement about 'what waits at home' as a topic — は frames it and often pairs with 〜とは限らない.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present it as new identifying info, clashing with the generic claim being made.

contrast_examples.jp: 待ってるのは人だけじゃない。

prompt.context_jp: 玄関を開けるより先に、ケンの足音___板の間を駆けてくるのがわかる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 玄関を開けるより先に、ケンの足音___板の間を駆けてくるのがわかる。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that best fits the blank.

feedback.correct_en: Inside a subordinate clause (〜のがわかる), subjects normally take が. Ken's footsteps are also new perceptual information.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside this kind of embedded perception clause sounds unnatural and would shift it to a contrastive reading.

contrast_examples.jp: 雨が降るのが聞こえる。
contrast_examples.en: I can hear the rain falling.

prompt.context_jp: 最初は我慢していたものの、時間とともに痛み___容赦なく強まっていく。
prompt.prompt_jp: 時間とともに痛み___容赦なく強まっていく。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that best fits the blank.

feedback.correct_en: The pain was already introduced ('最初は我慢していた'); now it continues as the established topic being described.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would reintroduce the pain as fresh new information, which doesn't fit — we're continuing a known topic.

contrast_examples.en: The pain (we're talking about) grew stronger.

prompt.context_jp: みちるの頭を占めていたの___自分の体のことより、家で待っているケンのことだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: みちるの頭を占めていたの___自分の体のことより、家で待っているケンのことだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that best fits the blank.

feedback.correct_en: 'What occupied her mind' is set up as the topic, then characterized ('…was Ken'). は fits the 〜のは〜だ structure.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would create an identifying cleft but with 〜より the natural flow uses は as topic frame.

prompt.context_jp: 「入院」という言葉に、桑野の眉___微かに動く。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「入院」という言葉に、桑野の眉___微かに動く。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that best fits the blank.

feedback.correct_en: A momentary visible reaction is described — the eyebrows twitch as newly observed action. が marks the subject of this sudden event.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'his eyebrows' a contrastive topic, which doesn't match a single neutral observation.

contrast_examples.en: His eyes are gentle. (description of topic)

prompt.context_jp: 空調の音だけ___、二人のあいだにしばらく残った。
prompt.prompt_jp: 空調の音だけ___、二人のあいだにしばらく残った。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that best fits the blank.

feedback.correct_en: 〜だけが emphasizes exhaustive listing: 'only the AC sound, and nothing else' remained. This is a classic が use after だけ.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけは would imply contrast with other things that didn't remain — awkward here. を is wrong since 残る is intransitive.

prompt.context_jp: 支払いを済ませ、袋___受け取ろうとしたところで、桑野は不意に肩越しの気配に気づいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 袋___受け取ろうとしたところで…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that best fits the blank.

feedback.correct_en: 受け取る is a transitive verb; its direct object (the bag being received) takes を.
feedback.incorrect_en: に would mark a destination/recipient, not the thing received. が would mark subject, not object.

contrast_examples.en: To hand a letter to him.

prompt.context_jp: 沙織の視線___だんだんと冷たくなっていくのを、鈍い英治もようやく感じ取り始めていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 沙織の視線___だんだんと冷たくなっていくのを…感じ取り始めていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that best fits the blank.

feedback.correct_en: Inside the 〜のを感じ取る embedded clause, the subject takes が. It's also presented as new observed change.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside this kind of nominalized perception clause would be ungrammatical / unnatural.

contrast_examples.jp: 風が強くなるのを感じた。
contrast_examples.en: I felt the wind growing stronger.

prompt.context_jp: 「ほかに病院は いくらでもあるでしょう？ でも この子___ ほかに行く所がないんです」
prompt.prompt_jp: でも この子___ ほかに行く所がないんです。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that best fits the blank.

feedback.correct_en: Natsumi contrasts the dog with hospitals: 'hospitals have alternatives, but THIS one (contrastively) has nowhere to go.' は marks the contrastive topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark new-info subject, losing the explicit contrast with the previous sentence.

contrast_examples.jp: ほかはいいが、これはダメだ。
contrast_examples.en: Others are fine, but this one is no good. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: ふと、ケン___低くうなり声を漏らした。
prompt.prompt_jp: ふと、ケン___低くうなり声を漏らした。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that best fits the blank.

feedback.correct_en: ふと signals a sudden event — Ken suddenly growling is new, observed action. Event subjects with ふと take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make Ken the established topic of commentary, not fitting a sudden burst. を is wrong because Ken is the subject.

prompt.context_jp: 手術___無事に終わり、病室のみちるはようやく目を覚ましつつあった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 手術___無事に終わり…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that best fits the blank.

feedback.correct_en: The surgery has been the central topic across preceding scenes; here it's wrapped up as the established theme ('as for the surgery, it ended well').
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present it as fresh new info, but readers have been following the surgery setup for many sentences.

contrast_examples.en: The exam (we knew about) is over.

prompt.context_jp: 「うちのマンション___ペット自由なんで ご心配なく」
prompt.prompt_jp: うちのマンション___ペット自由なんで ご心配なく。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that best fits the blank.

feedback.correct_en: 'As for our apartment, pets are free' — classic topic-comment structure. Also implicit contrast with other apartments that don't allow pets.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make the apartment new identifying info, awkward in this reassurance. を is ungrammatical here.

contrast_examples.en: As for us, the station is close.
A house whose station is close. (modifying)

prompt.context_jp: 犯人___もちろん、部屋の隅で神妙な顔をしている一匹だけである。
prompt.prompt_jp: 犯人___もちろん、部屋の隅で神妙な顔をしている一匹だけである。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that best fits the blank.

feedback.correct_en: 'As for the culprit, (it's) of course that one…' — 犯人 is the topic being characterized, a classic 〜は〜である frame.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make 犯人 an exhaustive-listing subject, but 犯人はもちろん〜 is the idiomatic framing here.

prompt.context_jp: 電話___鳴った。
prompt.prompt_jp: 電話___鳴った。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that best fits the blank.

feedback.correct_en: A classic 'the phone rang' scene-event sentence. The phone is new, sudden information — が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply 'as for the phone…' which sounds like commentary, not a sudden event. を is wrong for the subject.

prompt.context_jp: 「あなたと桑野さん 目___似てる」
prompt.prompt_jp: あなたと桑野さん 目___似てる。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that best fits the blank.

feedback.correct_en: 似ている takes が for the attribute that's similar. 'Eyes are what's similar' — exhaustive/identifying が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would read as contrastive ('eyes at least are similar') and sounds off here as a quiet observation. を is wrong because 似る is intransitive.

prompt.context_jp: そのとき、伸ばした指先が机の端をわずかに___。
prompt.prompt_jp: 伸ばした指先が机の端をわずかに___。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that best fits (lightly grazed).

feedback.correct_en: かすめる means to graze/brush lightly — matches わずかに (slightly) perfectly.
feedback.incorrect_en: 殴る (to punch) is too violent; 抱える (to hold/carry) doesn't fit a fingertip touching a desk edge.

prompt.context_jp: 「多分 ___虫垂炎ね」
prompt.prompt_jp: 多分 ___虫垂炎ね。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that best fits (likely acute appendicitis).

feedback.correct_en: 急性 (acute) fits appendicitis that hit suddenly and intensely this morning.
feedback.incorrect_en: 慢性 (chronic) contradicts the sudden onset. 陽性 (positive, as in test result) is a different medical category.

prompt.context_jp: 桑野の___拒絶の前に、英治はうなだれるしかなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 桑野の___拒絶の前に、英治はうなだれるしかなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that best fits (stubborn refusal).

feedback.correct_en: 頑な (stubborn/obstinate) fits Kuwano's unyielding rejection that forces Eiji to give up.
feedback.incorrect_en: 穏やか (calm) and 柔らか (soft) both contradict Eiji's reaction of hanging his head in defeat.

prompt.context_jp: 二人を追い返すこともできず、桑野は___、扉を大きく開いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 桑野は___、扉を大きく開いた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the expression that best fits (reluctantly).

feedback.correct_en: 不承不承 (reluctantly, unwillingly) fits Kuwano who can't refuse but doesn't want to let them in.
feedback.incorrect_en: 喜々として (joyfully) is the opposite. 堂々と (grandly) doesn't fit his grudging mood.

prompt.context_jp: 意外な返事に___、夏美は口を半ば開いたまま桑野を見た。
prompt.prompt_jp: 意外な返事に___、夏美は口を半ば開いたまま桑野を見た。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the expression (taken aback).

feedback.correct_en: 虚を突かれる (to be caught off guard) matches her open-mouthed surprise at an unexpected reply.
feedback.incorrect_en: 背を向ける (turn one's back) and 手を打つ (take action/clap) don't fit a reaction of shock.

contrast_examples.jp: 虚を突かれて言葉を失う。
contrast_examples.en: Caught off guard, she lost her words.

prompt.context_jp: 「仕事のパートナーとしては ここは ___しかないと思いまして」
prompt.prompt_jp: ここは ___しかないと思いまして。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the idiom (to pitch in / lend a hand).

feedback.correct_en: ひと肌脱ぐ is the set phrase for 'to help out / lend a hand for someone's sake' — exactly Sawazaki's offer.
feedback.incorrect_en: 手を引く means to withdraw (opposite meaning). 顔を出す means 'to make an appearance,' which doesn't match offering help.

contrast_examples.jp: 友のためにひと肌脱ぐ。
contrast_examples.en: To go the extra mile for a friend.

prompt.context_jp: 「預かってやった恩を忘れやがって ___やつだな ホントに」
prompt.prompt_jp: 預かってやった恩を忘れやがって ___やつだな。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the adjective (brazen / cheeky).

feedback.correct_en: ふてぶてしい (shameless/brazen) matches Kuwano's annoyance at the dog's defiant attitude.
feedback.incorrect_en: 初々しい (innocent/fresh) and 奥ゆかしい (modest/graceful) are the opposite — compliments, not complaints.

prompt.context_jp: 「ケンです！ ___分かってますよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: ケンです！ ___分かってますよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the phrase meaning 'without needing to be told'.

feedback.correct_en: 言われなくても (even without being told) is Kuwano's snappy retort — he already knows the dog's name.
feedback.incorrect_en: 言うまでもなく means 'needless to say,' used in neutral/formal statements, not a retort. 言いながら ('while saying') is grammatically off.

contrast_examples.en: I'll do it without being told.

contrast_examples.jp: 言うまでもなく大事だ。

prompt.context_jp: Michiru coming home to her dog — expressing that someone is waiting.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural for 'in my one-person apartment, there's someone who greets me with welcome home'?

choices.text: ひとり暮らしの部屋に、ただいまと呼びかけられる存在がいる。
ひとり暮らしの部屋は、ただいまと呼びかけられる存在をいる。

feedback.correct_en: Existence verb いる takes が for its subject, and locations take に. This matches the story's original line.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option B misuses は for the location and を for the subject of いる, both ungrammatical.

contrast_examples.en: There's a cat in the room.

contrast_examples.jp: 部屋には猫しかいない。
contrast_examples.en: In the room there's only a cat.

prompt.context_jp: Natsumi dismissing Kuwano's provocation about being lonely.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural to say 'there's no point arguing'?

choices.text: 議論してもしょうがないです。
議論するのもしょうがないです。

feedback.correct_en: 〜てもしょうがない is the fixed pattern meaning 'there's no point in doing X.' Option A matches the drama's line.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜のもしょうがない shifts meaning toward 'can't be helped that we do X,' which doesn't convey 'arguing is pointless.'

contrast_examples.jp: 心配してもしょうがない。
失敗したのはしょうがない。
contrast_examples.en: It can't be helped that we failed.

prompt.context_jp: Natsumi suggesting new experiences can be good.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural?

choices.text: ふだんしない経験するのもいいもんですよ。
ふだんしない経験するのがいいもんですよ。

feedback.correct_en: 〜のもいい suggests 'doing X too is good' — a gentle suggestion. This matches Natsumi's tone of mild persuasion.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜のがいい would assert 'X is the (best) thing to do,' which sounds too directive and doesn't fit the offering nuance.

contrast_examples.jp: たまには休むのもいい。
contrast_examples.en: Resting now and then is also good.
Resting is the thing to do.

prompt.context_jp: Natsumi reassuring Michiru that no news means Ken is safe.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more natural?

choices.text: 連絡がないってことは、無事だってことだしね。
連絡がないことが、無事なことだしね。

feedback.correct_en: 〜ってことは〜ってことだ is a very natural spoken pattern meaning 'the fact that X means Y.' Fits Natsumi's casual reassurance.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option B's 〜ことが〜ことだ sounds flat and unidiomatic — missing the inferential 'means that…' nuance.

contrast_examples.jp: 返事がないってことは、ダメってことだ。
contrast_examples.en: No reply means it's a no.

contrast_examples.jp: 返事がないのは残念だ。

prompt.context_jp: Kuwano advising Natsumi on walking the dog.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural for 'if you pull at your own convenience, it will follow along on its own'?

choices.text: 人の都合で引けば、勝手についてくるみたいですから。
人の都合に引けば、勝手についてくるみたいですから。

feedback.correct_en: 〜で (means/basis) marks how one pulls: 'by one's own convenience.' This matches the drama's line.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜に doesn't fit here — 都合に引く is not a natural collocation for 'pull based on one's own convenience.'

contrast_examples.en: To walk at one's own pace.

contrast_examples.jp: 相手のペースに合わせる。
contrast_examples.en: To match the other person's pace.
